# Upgrade upstream handling with new features (2025-12-05 10:33Z)

_**User (2025-12-05 10:32Z)**_

Upstream Handling Changes

**Current state (refs: src/upstream.ts, src/config.ts, src/stats.ts)**



Random selection among non-cooldown/non-blocked upstreams; no performance weighting or stickiness.

Failures (5xx/429/network) trigger a single fixed cooldown; daily-limit exhaustion triggers a 24h block; both are tracked in-memory only.

/api/statistics surfaces current in-memory pool state but resets on restart; no health probes or background retries.

Planned improvements (per asks)



Weighted load balancing: track per-upstream latency/success EWMA and pick faster/healthier upstreams more often; degrade weights for slow responders; respect daily limits (prefer fastest until quota hits) and optional light stickiness.

Distinct cooldowns: separate paths for (a) daily-limit exhaustion (24h block) and (b) HTTP 4xx/5xx/network failures using exponential backoff; store next retry timestamps separately.

Background recovery: periodic lightweight probes for failed/cooldown upstreams with jittered intervals to reintroduce them automatically after errors.

Statistics durability: keep /api/statistics up to date with weights, health, cooldown/backoff vs daily-limit block, next retry, and persisted counters so restarts don’t drop visibility.

Testing: add/extend unit + integration coverage for all new behaviours (weighted selection, cooldown split, probes, persistence, and stats exposure).

Todos



lb-weighted: Implement EWMA-based weighted picker (latency/success) replacing random selection; keep quota-aware fallback; add tests.

cooldown-split: Separate daily-limit block from error backoff with exponential timing; include next retry metadata; add tests.

bg-probes: Add background probes/retry scheduler for failed upstreams to rejoin the pool without client load; add tests.

stats-durable: Persist per-upstream counters/state for /api/statistics, exposing weights, cooldown/backoff, daily-limit blocks, and quotas; add tests.

**Explaining 403 handling and proposing patch**

The code treats 403 as non-failure due to shouldMarkFailure excluding <500 except 429, causing upstream retries to override client 403 with 500. To fix, I'll suggest disabling got retries and setting throwHttpErrors false in fetchTile, then manually throwing on 4xx/429/5xx statuses to mark failure and enable fallback. This ensures 403 is treated as failure and triggers other upstream attempts.</details></think>

(error) {\n    logger.error({ err: error }, 'transparent proxy upstream error');\n    if (!reply.sent) {\n      reply.code(502);\n      reply.send({ error: 'Upstream error' });\n    }\n  }\n};\n\nexport const createUpstreamMetricsProvider = async (\n  config: AppConfig,\n  redis?: Redis\n): Promise&lt;UpstreamMetricsProvider&gt; =&gt; {\n  const pool = getPool(config, redis);\n  await pool.ensureReady();\n  return {\n    describeUpstreams: () =&gt; pool.describe(config.upstreamDailyLimit)\n  };\n};\n"
